subject: Acme - follow-up: context-length profiling & pricing (prompt/completion tokens)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - follow-up: context-length profiling & pricing (prompt/completion tokens)

Hi Alex 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery: Acme is evaluating a retrieval-augmented generation workflow across product docs + customer transcripts, and latency/cost are the top gating factors. You mentioned potentially starting with a 100k monthly active user pilot and looking to estimate unit economics for production.

Action items I promised:
- Example pricing scenarios based on observed prompt/completion token distributions (8k/32k/128k context variants)
- A short questionnaire to get sample prompt/completion averages and % of flows that would need extended context (32k+, 128k)
- A sample MA-priced proposal for your procurement team (attached)

Two quick asks so I can model realistic pricing for the pilot:
1) Can you share approximate averages for the two primary flows we discussed (search+answer and chat assistant)? Ideally: avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens for each. If you only have distributions, ranges or percentiles (p50/p90) will work.
2) Out of all requests, what % do you expect to require: <=8k, 8k-32k, 32k-128k? (even rough ballpark numbers are fine e.g., 80/15/5)
3) Target unit economics e.g., do you have a target cost goal (e.g., $/1M tokens) or a monthly budget range for the pilot? If procurement prefers, a target total monthly spend also helps.

I attached the draft MA pricing proposal and a sample CSV you can drop numbers into (context-length-sample.csv). I'll run three scenarios (8k baseline, 32k mixed, 128k heavy) and show per-1M-token target pricing and expected monthly cost for your stated volumes.

If easier, feel free to reply inline or just paste a small sample of exports and I'll do the rest. 

Thanks 
I'll aim to get the scenarios back by Friday if I have the numbers today/early tomorrow.


Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: acme-ma-pricing-proposal.pdf (draft), context-length-sample.csv

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - follow-up: context-length profiling & pricing (prompt/completion tokens)

Marissa 

Great summary, and thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers below based on our current telemetry and rough estimates:

Search + answer (main product doc retrieval):
- avg prompt tokens: 420 (p50 ~380, p90 ~780)
- avg completion tokens: 180 (p50 ~120, p90 ~500)
- approx % by context need: <=8k: 95%, 8k-32k: 5%, 32k-128k: ~0%

Chat assistant (support-facing chat where we include recent conversation + relevant doc snippets):
- avg prompt tokens: 1,400 (p50 ~1,200, p90 ~3,600)
- avg completion tokens: 320 (p50 ~200, p90 ~1,200)
- approx % by context need: <=8k: 70%, 8k-32k: 25%, 32k-128k: 5%

Pilot sizing:
- Expected pilot traffic: ~100k MAU, ~1.2M requests/month (mix of both flows; split ~70% search, 30% chat)
- Ballpark monthly token volume: ~350M tokens/month (prompt + completions) 
- this is a rough internal estimate
- Procurement target: looking for conservative ops cost <$4000/month for the pilot (we have separate infra/dev budget), but flexible if we can see clear ROI/latency improvements.

Procurement looped in for contract/versioning terms. Let me know if you want raw logs or a small sample export; we can get that to you by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Product Manager, Search & Assist
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - follow-up: context-length profiling & pricing (prompt/completion tokens)

Alex 

This is perfect, thanks for the detail. I ran a quick back-of-envelope while we wait for any sample exports, and a few initial notes:

1) Unit economics: at Redwood we model pricing primarily per 1M tokens (token = input+output). For a pilot of ~350M tokens/mo your target of <$4000/mo would imply ~<$11.50 per 1M tokens (350M tokens * $11.50/1M = ~$4,025).
2) Practical ranges we typically see: hosted usage pricing ranges from ~$10-$40 / 1M tokens depending on SLOs, context length (higher for 128k), and optional caching/batching. Dedicated/committed capacity can bring that below $10/1M for high volumes.

I'll produce three scenarios based on your percentages and avg tokens:
- Scenario A (8k baseline): assume 95% search and 70% chat fall under <=8k. Cost estimate using default hosted SKU.
- Scenario B (32k mixed): includes the 8k-32k percentages you gave and adjusts per-token cost for longer context models (we apply a context multiplier for 32k requests).
- Scenario C (128k heavy): small % of 32k-128k requests (your chat 5%) modeled at premium pricing.

I'll attach a small table in the next note, showing: requests, prompt tokens, completion tokens, total tokens, cost @ $/1M (we'll run $8, $12, $20 comparisons) and a best-fit recommendation (Hosted vs Dedicated).

Two more quick Qs for accuracy:
- Do you expect any flows to use streaming completions? (those increase latency sensitivity but not token accounting)
- Any retention/PII constraints that would push you to Private deployment (affects pricing/licensing)?

I'll prep the scenarios and share by EOD tomorrow. If procurement prefers, I can include a committed-capacity quote that targets $8/1M for the pilot.

Marissa

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - follow-up: context-length profiling & pricing (prompt/completion tokens)

Marissa 

Answers to your quick Qs:
- Yes, chat assistant will use streaming in cases where we expect multi-part responses; search+answer will be non-streaming.
- No strict PII constraints for the pilot; we can use hosted with standard contract terms. Procurement will confirm any SOC2 evidence requests once we get the draft MA.

Procurement: feel free to review the attached draft and nominate next steps (SOW timeline, signatures) 
- happy to set a call next week if that helps.

If you can include the committed-capacity quote at $8/1M as an option, that would be ideal for our internal finance review.

Talk soon,
Alex
